[operator-attested] REBAR REVIEW-PLAN RAN GREEN AGAINST REAL BEDROCK — the remaining operator-attested AC.

Command: REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 AWS_PROFILE=frontier AWS_REGION=us-east-2 rebar review-plan 9249-1569-7be9-4f67 --ref HEAD --no-sign

Result: a VALID STRUCTURED VERDICT — PLAN REVIEW: BLOCK for 9249-1569-7be9-4f67, blocking=2 advisory=13 overflow=0 dropped=3 indeterminate=0. Exit 1 is the BLOCK verdict, i.e. the gate reached a decision; it is not an error. --no-sign was used deliberately so this exercise did not write an attestation onto an unrelated ticket.

This is materially stronger evidence than the cache canary recorded earlier: the canary is a single text-mode call, whereas review-plan drives the FULL agentic gate on Bedrock — the tool loop, the four-pass find/verify/decide/coach pipeline, structured output through the prompted path, and the capability layer this story added. It completing with a well-formed verdict means the whole first-class Bedrock path works end to end, not merely that a model answered.

It also exercised the temperature handling this story introduced: rebar Pass-2 verify steps send temperature=0, which is exactly the input that 400s on some Bedrock models, and the run completed.

GERRIT EVIDENCE for the lint/typecheck/suite criterion (my earlier comment predated the votes): commit 17a21ed21, change 1043 https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1043, which now carries **LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1** — CI independently ran build/test/lint/typecheck on this exact commit and agreed with the local run (make lint clean, mypy clean on 385 source files, full gating suite 7538 passed / 29 skipped / 115 deselected / exit 0).
